about.title: Morro Bay Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Morro Bay is small enough that one death touches more than one household. Fewer than eleven thousand people live here, and in 2025 the public record showed 26 injury collisions and 30 people hurt on local roads, with no traffic deaths logged that year. That is worth stating plainly, because wrongful death claims in a town like this often begin somewhere other than a crash: a fall on poorly maintained property, a medical error, an incident at work, or a collision involving a visitor unfamiliar with Route 1, Main Street, or South Bay Boulevard. Whatever the cause, California law gives a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or child the first right to bring a civil claim, and it sets a two-year clock from the date of death, shorter if a public agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We listen, then connect you with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death cases in San Luis Obispo County and works on contingency, so nothing is owed unless your family recovers something.

whyChoose.title: Why Morro Bay Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who may file
items.desc: California limits standing in wrongful death cases, placing a spouse, domestic partner, and children first, with certain dependents and heirs after them. The attorney we connect you with can tell you early whether you qualify and how relatives should coordinate a single claim.

items.title: Deadlines handled before they matter
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death to file, but that window shrinks sharply when a city, county, or state agency such as Caltrans may share fault. Getting counsel involved early keeps those dates from becoming a second loss.

items.title: A separate path from any criminal case
items.desc: A wrongful death claim is a civil action, independent of whatever prosecutors do or do not pursue. It can address funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance your family has suffered.

items.question: Our relative was killed in a collision on Route 1 near Morro Bay. Does the location change anything?
items.answer: It can. Route 1 is a state highway, so if road design, signage, or maintenance played any role, a government entity may be a potential defendant, and claims against public agencies carry a much shorter filing deadline than the standard two years. An attorney will want to look at that question quickly, alongside the more common issue of the other driver's conduct and insurance.

items.question: The person responsible is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death lawsuit is a civil matter that runs on its own track, and the two-year deadline keeps running regardless of what happens in criminal court. Your attorney may use evidence from the criminal case, but the civil claim does not depend on a conviction, and the standards of proof are different.

items.question: What does LawProactive actually do, and what does it cost our family?
items.answer: We are a free service, not a law firm. After you reach out, we connect you with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death cases in San Luis Obispo County, and that attorney works on contingency, meaning no legal fee is owed unless there is a recovery. There is no charge from us at any point.
